thesis: Deployed models require causal evidence, calibrated evaluation and layered defenses against deliberate manipulation and privacy leakage.
role: Extend reliability beyond offline prediction into interventions, graders and adversaries.

ideas.statement: Prediction does not estimate what an intervention will change; randomized experiments and explicit causal assumptions are needed.
Open-ended evaluation needs checkable tasks or explicit rubrics, judges tested against experts, uncertainty estimates and fresh private user questions.
Adversarial examples, data poisoning and prompt injection exploit different stages; narrow permissions and checks limit agent consequences.
Memorization and membership inference leak private information; differential privacy accounts for cumulative disclosure and federated learning alone is insufficient.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: The rooster predicts sunrise without causing it, while wine judges demonstrate why evaluators must themselves be tested.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: Observational causal methods require assumptions, and injection defenses reduce risk without a general guarantee.

audit.notes: Entire assigned segment reviewed; scope and qualifications preserved. Duplicate contents and publication metadata are not ranked as ideas.
